title: Little Women
events_chronological: The four March sisters perform Jo's play in the attic on Christmas Eve and then give their breakfast away to a starving family down the road.
Jo meets their neighbour Laurie at a ball while hiding a scorch mark in the back of her dress.
Amy is caned in front of her class for keeping pickled limes and is taken out of school.
Amy burns Jo's manuscript, and Jo tells her she will never forgive her as long as she lives.
Amy goes through the ice on the river and Jo, having nearly let her drown, forgives her.
Old Mr Laurence gives Beth his dead daughter's piano.
A telegram says their father is wounded, and Jo sells her hair to pay for their mother's journey to him.
Beth catches scarlet fever from the family they have been feeding and very nearly dies of it.
Meg marries John Brooke in the garden with almost no money and is happy about it.
Laurie proposes to Jo and Jo turns him down, telling him they would kill each other.
Jo sells sensational stories to a New York paper under a false name while her lodging-house neighbour, a German professor, tells her plainly that they are not good.
Amy studies painting in Europe under the eye of Aunt March and meets Laurie again, drunk and idle.
Meg, poor and married, buys fifty dollars of silk she cannot afford and confesses it to John.
Word comes that Beth is dying, and Jo goes home to nurse her by the sea.
Beth dies, and Jo shuts herself in the attic and begins writing the story of the four of them.
Amy and Laurie marry abroad and come home together, and Jo's letter offering herself to Laurie arrives too late.
Jo argues the ending and the copyright out of the publisher Mr Dashwood, and the book is set in type.
syuzhet_notes: The film cuts between the childhood years and the present on a regular beat, matching each pair: the two Christmases, the two scenes at Beth's bedside, the two attics. The beat loosens in the last third as the past catches up with the present.
fabula_notes: The childhood strand is seven years earlier throughout, distinguished by warmer light and by which sisters are in the house. The publisher's negotiation is the latest event in the story.
